Algebra I · Lesson 6.5

Direct and Inverse Proportion

Solve this lesson →All lessons

A ratio compares two amounts at one moment. This lesson is about two amounts that both change, and about the combination of them that stays fixed while they do. Sometimes that combination is the quotient of the two amounts, the same number at every moment. Sometimes it is the product. The first two problems have a fixed quotient.

Problem
A press stamps tags out of sheets of metal, and every sheet gives the same number of tags. A run of 12 sheets gives 84 tags. A later run uses 36 sheets. Enter the number of tags the later run gives.
Show a hint
  • Every sheet gives the same number of tags, so the two runs differ only in how many sheets went through. Compare 36 sheets with 12 sheets.
  • 36÷12=336÷12=3, so the later run is three copies of the first run.
Show the full solution
The later run uses 36÷12=336÷12=3 times as many sheets, and every sheet gives the same number of tags, so the tag count is 3(84)=2523(84)=252​. How many tags one sheet gives was never needed, only the fact that it does not change.
Problem
The same press, the same sheets, so 12 sheets still give 84 tags. A new run uses 55 sheets, and 55 is not a whole number of twelves. Work out how many tags one sheet gives first, then enter the number of tags the 55-sheet run gives.
Show a hint
  • The 12-sheet run gives 84 tags and every sheet gives the same number, so one sheet's share is a division.
  • 84÷12=784÷12=7 tags per sheet, and the run has 55 sheets.
Show the full solution
One sheet gives 84÷12=784÷12=7 tags, so 55 sheets give 7×55=3857×55=385​. Working out the per-sheet count first handles any run, while multiplying the 12-sheet run by a whole-number factor only works when the new sheet count is a multiple of 12.
Key idea
Direct proportion. Two amounts xx and yy are directly proportional when yxxy​ is the same number at every matching pair. That number is kk, the constant of proportionality. Multiplying yx=kxy​=k by xx gives y=kxy=kx, and dividing y=kxy=kx by xx gives yx=kxy​=k back, so the two forms say the same thing. One division at a known pair gives kk, and the yy at any other xx is then kxkx. For the press, k=7k=7 tags per sheet.
Problem
The mass of a steel sheet is directly proportional to its area. A sheet of area 18 square meters has mass 234 kilograms. Enter the mass in kilograms of a sheet of area 31 square meters.
Show a hint
  • Here kk is the mass of one square meter of the steel. The 18 square meter sheet is enough to find it.
  • 234÷18=13234÷18=13, so every square meter has mass 13 kilograms.
Show the full solution
k=234÷18=13k=234÷18=13 kilograms per square meter, so the larger sheet has mass 13(31)=40313(31)=403​. Going from 18 straight to 31 without kk means multiplying 234 by 31181831​, which is not a whole number, so finding kk first keeps every step in whole numbers.
Problem
Dyeing fabric uses an amount of dye directly proportional to the mass of the fabric. Dyeing 14 kilograms of fabric uses 6 grams of dye. Enter the number of grams of dye needed for 35 kilograms of the same fabric.
Show a hint
  • kk is the dye used per kilogram of fabric, and it is not a whole number here.
  • 614=37146​=73​ grams per kilogram, and 35 is a multiple of 7.
Show the full solution
k=614=37k=146​=73​ grams of dye per kilogram of fabric, so 35 kilograms need 37(35)=1573​(35)=15​. A constant of proportionality is a rate, and there is no reason a rate should come out whole. Scaling gives the same value, since 35÷14=5235÷14=25​ and 52(6)=1525​(6)=15.
Key idea
Two routes through a direct proportion. One route is to compute k=yxk=xy​ at the known pair and then multiply the new xx by kk. The other is to multiply the known yy by mm, where mm is the new xx divided by the known xx. Both give the same value, since y=kxy=kx with xx replaced by mxmx is k(mx)=m(kx)k(mx)=m(kx), which is mm times the old yy. Scaling is shorter when one xx divides the other evenly. Finding kk works whatever the two values are, and the extra division is worth it when several questions about the same relationship follow.

A fixed quotient is one way for two amounts to vary together. A fixed product is the other. Cut a strip into equal pieces and the number of pieces times the length of one piece is the length of the whole strip every time, so more pieces means shorter pieces. Two amounts whose product is the same at every pair are inversely proportional.

Problem
All the chairs in a hall are set out in rows, with the same number of chairs in every row, and every arrangement uses all of the chairs. One arrangement is 18 rows of 42 chairs. Another arrangement has 27 rows. Enter the number of chairs in each row of the 27-row arrangement.
Show a hint
  • Both arrangements use the same chairs, so the number of rows times the number of chairs in each row comes out the same both times.
  • 27 rows is 3223​ times 18 rows, so each row of the 27-row arrangement holds 2332​ as many chairs.
Show the full solution
From 18 rows to 27 rows the row count is multiplied by 2718=321827​=23​, so the number in each row is divided by that same factor, giving 42÷32=2842÷23​=28​. The product of the two counts is fixed at 18(42)=75618(42)=756, which is what inverse proportion means here, and 756÷27=28756÷27=28 confirms it.
Problem
On a level balance beam, the mass hung on one side times its distance from the pivot is the same number for every load that balances the beam. A 27 kilogram mass balances it at 16 centimeters from the pivot. Enter the distance in centimeters at which a 12 kilogram mass balances the same beam.
Show a hint
  • The fixed number here is a mass times its distance from the pivot, and the 27 kilogram load gives it.
  • 27(16)=43227(16)=432, so mass times distance is 432 for any load that balances.
Show the full solution
k=27(16)=432k=27(16)=432, so the 12 kilogram mass balances at 432÷12=36432÷12=36​. The lighter mass sits further from the pivot because the product has to stay 432. Scaling agrees, since the mass is multiplied by 1227=492712​=94​ and 16÷49=3616÷94​=36.
Key idea
Inverse proportion. Two amounts xx and yy are inversely proportional when the product xyxy is the same number at every matching pair. That number is again kk, so xy=kxy=k, and dividing by xx gives y=kxy=xk​. One multiplication at a known pair gives kk. Multiplying xx by mm divides yy by mm, since kmx=1m⋅kxmxk​=m1​⋅xk​, so a larger xx always goes with a smaller yy while the product stays kk.

A description or a table of pairs does not say which relationship holds, so test it. Divide yy by xx at each pair and see whether one number comes out every time. Multiply xx by yy at each pair and do the same. At most one of the two tests passes, and for some amounts that vary together neither one does.

Problem
A table lists three pairs from one relationship. x81220y453018xy​845​1230​2018​​ Decide whether yy is directly proportional to xx or inversely proportional to xx, then enter the value of yy when x=40x=40.
Show a hint
  • Run both tests on the first two pairs. Only one of yxxy​ and xyxy repeats.
  • 8(45)=3608(45)=360 and 12(30)=36012(30)=360, so check the third pair against 360 as well.
Show the full solution
The quotients 458845​, 30121230​ and 18202018​ are three different numbers, while 8(45)8(45), 12(30)12(30) and 20(18)20(18) are all 360, so xy=360xy=360 and y=360÷40=9y=360÷40=9​. One pair can never settle which relationship holds, since a single pair has both a quotient and a product. Two pairs are the least that can rule one out.
Fun fact
In 1662 Robert Boyle poured mercury into a J-shaped tube, squeezing air trapped in the short closed arm. The readings gave his law that a fixed amount of gas at fixed temperature has volume inversely proportional to its pressure.
Problem
A taxi company charges the same way for every trip. A 5 kilometre trip costs 17 dollars and a 12 kilometre trip costs 31 dollars. Test whether the fare is directly proportional to the distance, or inversely proportional, before assuming either. Enter the cost in dollars of a 20 kilometre trip.
Show a hint
  • Test the two given trips. 175517​ and 31121231​ are different, and 17(5)17(5) and 31(12)31(12) are different, so neither the quotient nor the product is fixed.
  • The extra 7 kilometres between the two trips cost 31−17=1431−17=14 dollars, and the pickup charge is the same on both trips.
Show the full solution
The extra 7 kilometres cost 31−17=1431−17=14 dollars, so each kilometre costs 14÷7=214÷7=2 dollars, the pickup charge is 17−5(2)=717−5(2)=7 dollars, and 20 kilometres costs 20(2)+7=4720(2)+7=47​. Neither yxxy​ nor xyxy is fixed here, since 175517​ and 31121231​ differ and so do 17(5)17(5) and 31(12)31(12), so the fare is proportional to neither. Assuming direct proportion and multiplying the 5 kilometre fare by 4 gives 68, which charges the 7 dollar pickup four times over instead of once.
Key idea
The doubling test. Double xx and compare the new yy with the old one. Under y=kxy=kx the new value is k(2x)=2kxk(2x)=2kx, which is twice the old yy. Under y=kxy=xk​ it is k2x2xk​, which is half the old yy. If neither happens, the two amounts are proportional in neither sense, however closely they are related. The taxi fare is that case. At double the distance a fare of 2x+72x+7 dollars for xx kilometres is 4x+74x+7, while twice the fare would be 4x+144x+14.

The comparison can be with a power of xx. Saying yy is directly proportional to x2x2 means yx2x2y​ is the same number at every pair, so y=kx2y=kx2. Saying yy is inversely proportional to x2x2 means yx2yx2 is the same number at every pair, so y=kx2y=x2k​. One known pair still gives kk.

Problem
The area of a badge is directly proportional to the square of its height. A badge 6 centimeters tall has area 27 square centimeters. A second badge of the same shape is 14 centimeters tall. Enter its area in square centimeters.
Show a hint
  • The constant here is the area divided by the square of the height, not the area divided by the height, so divide 2727 by 6262 rather than by 66.
  • 2736=343627​=43​, and 142=196142=196.
Show the full solution
The constant is k=2762=2736=34k=6227​=3627​=43​, so the taller badge has area 34(142)=34(196)=14743​(142)=43​(196)=147​. Dividing 2727 by 66 instead gives 4.54.5 and then 6363, which would be the answer if the area were proportional to the height rather than to its square.
Problem
A meter reads the light falling on a screen, and the reading is inversely proportional to the square of the screen's distance from the lamp. At a distance of 3 metres the meter reads 400 units. Enter the reading at a distance of 15 metres.
Show a hint
  • Inversely proportional to the square of the distance means the reading times the square of the distance is the same number at every distance, not the reading times the distance.
  • The distance is multiplied by 15÷3=515÷3=5, so the square of the distance is multiplied by 2525.
Show the full solution
The distance is multiplied by 15÷3=515÷3=5, so the reading is divided by 52=2552=25, giving 400÷25=16400÷25=16​. Finding k=400(32)=3600k=400(32)=3600 and computing 36001521523600​ gives 16 as well, with larger numbers. Dividing by 5 rather than 25 gives 80, which is what scaling by the distance instead of by its square produces.
Key idea
Proportional to a power. yy is directly proportional to xnxn when yxnxny​ is the same number at every pair, so y=kxny=kxn, and inversely proportional to xnxn when yxnyxn is the same number at every pair, so y=kxny=xnk​. Multiplying xx by mm multiplies xnxn by mnmn, so yy is multiplied by mnmn in the direct case and divided by it in the inverse one. Tripling a length multiplies an area by 99 and a volume by 2727. Read backwards, the factor on yy is mnmn, so mm is its square root when n=2n=2 and its cube root when n=3n=3.

When only a factor is wanted, kk never has to be found. Under direct proportion, multiplying xx by a number multiplies yy by that same number. Under inverse proportion it divides yy by that number. With a power of xx, the factor is raised to that power before it is used. The last two problems are much shorter this way.

Problem
A rectangle is reshaped with its area kept the same, so its length and its width are inversely proportional. The length is changed to 5885​ of what it was. Enter the number the width is multiplied by, as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • No length, width or area is given, so the constant kk cannot be found. Work from the fact that the product of length and width is the same before and after.
  • Let the old length and width be LL and WW, and let the width be multiplied by cc. The old area is LWLW and the new area is 58L⋅cW85​L⋅cW, and those two are equal.
Show the full solution
The product of length and width is the same before and after, so if the length is multiplied by 5885​, the width must be divided by 5885​, and dividing by 5885​ is the same as multiplying by 8558​​. No length, width or area was given, so kk is unknown here, and the factor was found without it.
Problem
Storage bins in one product line all have the same shape. For that shape the outside surface area is directly proportional to the square of the height, and the volume is directly proportional to the cube of the height. A bin 10 centimetres tall has surface area 280 square centimetres and volume 300 cubic centimetres. A larger bin of the same shape has volume 2400 cubic centimetres. Enter its surface area in square centimetres.
Show a hint
  • The height of the larger bin is not given, so work in factors instead. Both volumes are known, so start by dividing one by the other.
  • The volume is multiplied by 2400÷300=82400÷300=8, and the volume is proportional to the cube of the height.
Show the full solution
The volume is multiplied by 2400÷300=82400÷300=8, and volume is proportional to the cube of the height, so the height is multiplied by 2 because 23=823=8. Surface area is proportional to the square of the height, so it is multiplied by 22=422=4, giving 280(4)=1120280(4)=1120​. Multiplying 280 by 8 instead gives 2240, but 8 is the volume factor and a surface area is two lengths multiplied together, so the height factor of 2 belongs in the product twice and not three times. A 6 by 5 by 10 box has volume 300 and surface area 280, and doubling every edge gives 2400 and 1120.

Most of these problems came down to one fixed number, found from one pair and then used on another, or skipped when only a factor was wanted. The taxi fare needed two, which put it outside both kinds of proportion. Lesson 6.6, Joint Proportion and Rates, has one amount varying with two others at once, so the statement is x=kyzx=kyz.

Practice these ideas

Practice
The cost of nylon rope is directly proportional to its length. A 7 meter piece costs 42 dollars. Enter the cost of a 35 meter piece of the same rope, in dollars.
Show the solution
k=42÷7=6k=42÷7=6 dollars per meter, so 35 meters cost 6(35)=2106(35)=210​. As a check, 35 meters is five 7 meter pieces, and 5(42)=2105(42)=210.
Practice
yy is directly proportional to xx, and y=51y=51 when x=17x=17. Enter the value of yy when x=23x=23.
Show the solution
k=5117=3k=1751​=3, so y=3xy=3x and y=3(23)=69y=3(23)=69​. Since 23 is not a multiple of 17, there is no whole-number scaling between the two pairs, and y=3xy=3x is true at every xx, including this one.
Practice
xx and yy are inversely proportional, and y=24y=24 when x=11x=11. Enter the value of yy when x=33x=33.
Show the solution
k=24(11)=264k=24(11)=264, so y=264÷33=8y=264÷33=8​. Tripling xx from 11 to 33 makes yy a third of what it was, so 24÷3=824÷3=8 gives the same answer without finding kk.
Practice
A fixed volume of soup is ladled out equally into bowls, with none left over. Enter the word direct or the word inverse for the relationship between the number of bowls and the amount of soup in each bowl.
Show the solution
The number of bowls times the amount in each bowl equals the fixed total, so the amount in each bowl is the total divided by the number of bowls, which makes the relationship inverseinverse​. Doubling the number of bowls halves the amount in each, while in a direct proportion doubling one would double the other.
Practice
yy is directly proportional to xx, and y=21y=21 when x=6x=6. Enter the constant of proportionality kk as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
k=216=72k=621​=27​​. A constant of proportionality is a rate, so a fraction is a perfectly ordinary value for it.
Practice
The mass of a bar of alloy is directly proportional to its length. A bar 26 centimeters long has mass 65 grams. Enter the length in centimeters of a bar of the same alloy with mass 100 grams.
Show the solution
The constant of proportionality is 6526=522665​=25​ grams per centimeter, so the length is 100÷52=40100÷25​=40​. Scaling works too, since the mass is multiplied by 10065=201365100​=1320​ and 26⋅2013=4026⋅1320​=40.
Practice
yy is inversely proportional to xx, and y=14y=14 when x=6x=6. Enter the value of xx when y=4y=4.
Show the solution
xy=14(6)=84xy=14(6)=84 for every pair, so 4x=844x=84 and x=21x=21​. Dividing yy by 7227​ to get from 1414 to 44 multiplies xx by 7227​, and 6⋅72=216⋅27​=21 as well.
Practice
A fixed load of gravel fills 24 barrows when each barrow carries 35 kilograms. Enter the number of kilograms in each barrow when the same load is spread evenly over 42 barrows.
Show the solution
The whole load is 24(35)=84024(35)=840 kilograms, and spread over 42 barrows that gives 840÷42=20840÷42=20​. Check, 42(20)=84042(20)=840 kilograms, the same load. Barrow count times kilograms per barrow stays fixed, which is what inverse proportion means.
Practice
A table lists three pairs from one relationship. x3712y122848xy​312​728​1248​​ Decide whether yy is directly proportional to xx or inversely proportional to xx, then enter the value of yy when x=20x=20.
Show the solution
All three quotients equal 4 while the products 36, 196 and 576 differ, so y=4xy=4x and y=4(20)=80y=4(20)=80​. Checking only one pair proves nothing, since a single pair has both a quotient and a product.
Practice
A fixed number of tiles is laid in rows of equal length, so the number of rows and the number of tiles in each row are inversely proportional. The number of rows is tripled. Enter the number that the tile count in each row is multiplied by, as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Writing the new counts as 3r3r rows and nn tiles per row, 3r⋅n=rt3r⋅n=rt gives n=t3n=3t​, so the tile count in each row is multiplied by 1331​​. The factors 33 and 1331​ multiply to 11, which is what keeps the total the same.
Practice
yy is directly proportional to x2x2, and y=48y=48 when x=4x=4. Enter the value of yy when x=9x=9.
Show the solution
k=4842=3k=4248​=3, so y=3(92)=243y=3(92)=243​. Using k=484=12k=448​=12 instead gives 12(9)=10812(9)=108, which is the answer only if yy is proportional to xx rather than to x2x2.
Practice
yy is inversely proportional to x2x2, and y=50y=50 when x=3x=3. Enter the value of yy when x=5x=5.
Show the solution
The constant yx2yx2 equals 50(32)=45050(32)=450, so y=45025=18y=25450​=18​. Ignoring the square and using yx=150yx=150 gives 3030 instead.
Practice
A courier charges a fixed handling amount plus a further amount for each kilogram. A 4 kilogram parcel costs 29 dollars and a 9 kilogram parcel costs 54 dollars. Enter the cost in dollars of a 15 kilogram parcel.
Show the solution
The extra 5 kilograms cost 54−29=2554−29=25 dollars, so each kilogram costs 5 dollars, the handling amount is 29−4(5)=929−4(5)=9 dollars, and a 15 kilogram parcel costs 15(5)+9=8415(5)+9=84​. Scaling 29 by 154415​ gives 108.75, too high because the 9 dollar handling amount is then counted 3.75 times instead of once.
Practice
For solid cubes cut from one material, the mass is directly proportional to the cube of the edge length. Such a cube with edge length 2 centimetres has mass 56 grams. Enter the mass in grams of a cube of the same material with edge length 5 centimetres.
Show the solution
k=5623=7k=2356​=7 grams per cubic centimetre, so the cube with edge length 5 centimetres has mass 7(125)=8757(125)=875​. Scaling the edge by 5225​ scales the mass by (52)3=1258(25​)3=8125​, and 56⋅1258=87556⋅8125​=875 as well.
Practice
The reading on a light meter is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the meter to the lamp. The meter is moved so that this distance becomes 2552​ of what it was. Enter the number the reading is multiplied by, as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
The denominator d2d2 is multiplied by (25)2=425(52​)2=254​, so the reading is divided by 425254​, the same as multiplying by 254425​​. Leaving out the square gives 5225​, the common wrong answer.
Practice
Among statues of one shape, mass is directly proportional to the cube of the height. One such statue is 40 centimeters tall and has mass 33 kilograms. A second statue of that shape has mass 891 kilograms. Enter the height of the second statue in centimeters.
Show the solution
The mass is multiplied by 891÷33=27891÷33=27, and mass is proportional to the cube of the height, so the height is multiplied by the number whose cube is 27, namely 3, giving 40(3)=12040(3)=120​. The check is that 1203=17280001203=1728000 is 27 times 403=64000403=64000. The common slip is 40(27)=108040(27)=1080, but 27 is the factor for the mass and 3 is the factor for the height.
Practice
A table lists three pairs from one relationship. x236y67530075xy​2675​3300​675​​ Neither yxxy​ nor xyxy is the same at every pair, but yy is inversely proportional to a power of xx. Enter the value of yy when x=5x=5.
Show the solution
The products yx2yx2 are 675(4)675(4), 300(9)300(9) and 75(36)75(36), all 2700, so yx2=2700yx2=2700 and y=270025=108y=252700​=108​. Doubling xx from 3 to 6 leaves yy at a quarter of its value rather than a half, which is what makes the power 2 and not 1.
